title: Exponents
summary: Write numbers in exponential form, work with squares, cubes and their roots, apply the laws of exponents for natural-number exponents, and write large numbers in scientific notation.

notes.text: Exponential form
An **exponent** tells you how many times a number is multiplied by itself. Instead of $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$ we write $2^5$, read as "2 to the power 5".

notes.caption: a is the base and n is the exponent

notes.text: In $5^3$, $5$ is the **base** and $3$ is the **exponent** (or index). The whole expression is called a **power**. $5^3 = 5 \times 5 \times 5 = 125$.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: $5^3$ does **not** mean $5 \times 3$. $5^3 = 125$, but $5 \times 3 = 15$.
Squares, cubes and roots
A number to the power 2 is a **square** and a number to the power 3 is a **cube**. Finding a root is the opposite (inverse) of squaring or cubing.
$\sqrt{49} = 7$ because $7^2 = 49$. The square root asks: "Which number, multiplied by itself, gives this?"
$\sqrt[3]{64} = 4$ because $4^3 = 64$. The cube root of a negative number is negative: $\sqrt[3]{-27} = -3$.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Parts (b) and (c) show that $\sqrt{9 + 16} \neq \sqrt{9} + \sqrt{16}$. You may not take the root of each term separately when they are added.
The laws of exponents
In Grade 8 the exponents are natural numbers. Each law can be explained by writing out the factors. For example, $x^2 \times x^3 = (x \times x)(x \times x \times x) = x^5$.

notes.caption: Laws of exponents (m and n natural numbers)
rows: Multiplying powers with the same base
Dividing powers with the same base

notes.text: Why is $x^0 = 1$? Use the division law: $\dfrac{x^3}{x^3} = x^{3-3} = x^0$. But anything divided by itself is $1$, so $x^0 = 1$.

notes.title: Worked example 2: simplifying
steps: (a) Multiply the numbers and add the exponents of $a$: $10a^{3+4} = 10a^7$.
(b) Divide the numbers and subtract the exponents: $3x^{6-2}y^{4-1} = 3x^4y^3$.

notes.label: Common mistakes
notes.text:
• $3^2 \times 3^4 = 3^6$, **not** $9^6$. Keep the base.
• $(2x)^3 = 8x^3$, **not** $2x^3$. The exponent applies to the $2$ as well.
• $a^2 + a^3 \neq a^5$. The laws are for multiplying and dividing, not for adding.
Comparing and calculating with powers
To compare powers, calculate them or write them with the same base. For example, $2^6$ and $4^3$: $4^3 = (2^2)^3 = 2^6$, so they are equal ($64$).

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: $(-1)$ to an even power is $1$ and to an odd power is $-1$. Any power of $1$ is $1$.
Scientific notation for large numbers
Very large numbers, such as distances in space or the population of a country, are written in **scientific notation**: a number between $1$ and $10$ multiplied by a power of $10$.

notes.title: Worked example 4
notes.problem: (a) Write $4\ 560\ 000$ in scientific notation.  (b) Write $3{,}2 \times 10^5$ as an ordinary number.
steps: (a) Place the decimal comma after the first digit: $4{,}56$. Count how many places it moved: $6$. So $4\ 560\ 000 = 4{,}56 \times 10^6$.
(b) Multiply by $10^5$: move the comma $5$ places to the right: $320\ 000$.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: $45{,}6 \times 10^5$ is **not** in scientific notation, because $45{,}6$ is not between $1$ and $10$. Correct it to $4{,}56 \times 10^6$.

notes.title: Worked example 5: a real-life problem
notes.problem: The population of South Africa is about $62\ 000\ 000$. Write this in scientific notation.

notes.text: Summary

items: Know the squares up to $12^2 = 144$ and the cubes up to $6^3 = 216$; roots undo powers.
Same base: multiply → add exponents; divide → subtract exponents; power of a power → multiply exponents.

questions.explanation: Same base, multiplying: add the exponents. $3 + 4 = 7$.
$3^2 + 4^2 = 9 + 16 = 25$, but $7^2 = 49$. You cannot add the bases.
Power of a power: multiply the exponents. $4 \times 3 = 12$.
The first number must be between $1$ and $10$: $4{,}56$. The comma moves 6 places, so $\times 10^6$.

questions.prompt: Match each expression with its value.
questions.explanation: $2^3 = 8$; $3^2 = 9$; $7^2 = 49$; $4^3 = 64$; any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1.
The exponent applies to every factor in the bracket: $(2x)^3 = 2^3x^3 = 8x^3$.

questions.prompt: Simplify $y^{10} \div y^2$ and give only the exponent of $y$ in your answer.
questions.explanation: Same base, dividing: subtract the exponents. $10 - 2 = 8$, so $y^8$.

questions.prompt:
The distance from the Earth to the Sun is about $149\ 600\ 000$ km.
(a) Write this distance in scientific notation.  (1)
(b) The Moon is about $3{,}84 \times 10^5$ km from the Earth. Write this as an ordinary number.  (1)
(c) Which is further from the Earth, the Sun or the Moon? Explain using the powers of ten.  (1)
